title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on Establishing and Improving a Mechanism for the Convergence of Litigation and Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Several Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Mechanism for Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 45

All local people's courts at various levels, all military courts at various levels, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, all maritime courts, and all courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The "Several Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Mechanism for Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution" of the Supreme People's Court has been approved by the Central Committee. It is hereby issued to you for earnest implementation. If problems arise during implementation, please promptly report them to the Office of the Judicial Reform Leading Group of the Supreme People's Court.

July 24, 2009

Several Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Mechanism for Linking Litigation and Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution

To give full play to the active role of the people's courts in establishing and improving the mechanism for linking litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution, and to promote the development of various dispute resolution mechanisms, the following opinions are hereby formulated.

I. Clarify Main Objectives and Task Requirements

1. The main objective of establishing and improving the mechanism for linking litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution is to fully utilize the strength of the people's courts, administrative organs, social organizations, enterprises, institutions, and all other parties, to promote mutual cooperation, coordination, and comprehensive development among various dispute resolution methods, to ensure the effective connection between litigation and non-litigation channels, to provide the people with more alternative dispute resolution options, to maintain social harmony and stability, and to promote sound and rapid economic and social development.

2. The main task of establishing and improving the mechanism for linking litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution is to fully leverage the normative, guiding, and supervisory role of adjudicative power, to improve the connection mechanism between litigation and arbitration, administrative mediation, people's mediation, commercial mediation, industry mediation, and other non-litigation dispute resolution methods, to promote the organizational and procedural institutional development of various dispute resolution mechanisms, to make non-litigation dispute resolution methods more convenient, flexible, and efficient, and to provide judicial guarantees for the prosperous development of dispute resolution mechanisms.

3. In the process of establishing and improving the mechanism for linking litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution, it is necessary to rely firmly on the leadership of the Party committee, actively seek government support, encourage participation from all sectors of society, and fully leverage the driving role of the judiciary; it is necessary to fully protect the parties' right to dispose of their civil rights and litigation rights in accordance with the law.

II. Promote the Development of Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution Mechanisms

4. Earnestly implement the Arbitration Law of the PRC and relevant judicial interpretations. In aspects such as the validity of arbitration agreements, rules of evidence, arbitration procedures, basis for awards, standards for review of setting aside awards, and standards for review of refusal to enforce awards, respect and reflect the unique principles of the arbitration system, and maximize the role of the arbitration system in dispute resolution. For applications for evidence preservation or property preservation during the arbitration process, the people's court shall handle them promptly in accordance with the law.

5. Earnestly implement the Labor Dispute Mediation and Arbitration Law of the PRC and the provisions of relevant judicial interpretations, strengthen communication and coordination with labor and personnel dispute arbitration institutions, adopt appropriate trial methods based on the characteristics of labor and personnel dispute cases, and support and encourage the role of arbitration mechanisms. For labor and personnel dispute matters that are not accepted by the labor and personnel dispute arbitration institution or for which no decision is made within the time limit, if the applicant files a lawsuit with the people's court, the people's court shall accept it in accordance with the law.

6. Further strengthen communication and coordination with rural land contract arbitration institutions, properly handle rural land contract disputes, and strive to provide strong judicial guarantees and legal services for rural reform and development. If a party is dissatisfied with the ruling of the rural land contract arbitration institution and files a lawsuit, the people's court shall hear it promptly. If a party applies to the court for enforcement of a legally effective award or mediation statement, the people's court shall enforce it promptly in accordance with the law.

7. The people's court shall vigorously support and supervise the mediation work of people's mediation organizations in accordance with the law. When hearing civil cases involving people's mediation agreements, the relevant legal provisions shall apply.

8. To effectively resolve various types of disputes arising in administrative management activities, the people's court encourages and supports administrative organs to conduct mediation, make rulings, or take other actions in accordance with the law upon the application of the parties or ex officio. Such mediation, rulings, or other actions taken in accordance with the law have legal effect. If a party is dissatisfied with the mediation, ruling, or other action taken by an administrative organ regarding a civil dispute between equal parties, and files a lawsuit with the people's court against the other party regarding the original dispute, the people's court shall accept it as a civil case. If the law or judicial interpretation clearly stipulates that it shall be accepted as an administrative case, the people's court may, when reviewing the administrative act, concurrently try the civil dispute therein and, while rendering the administrative judgment, also render a civil judgment in accordance with the law on the civil dispute between the parties.

A mediation agreement containing civil rights and obligations content reached after an administrative organ mediates a civil dispute in accordance with the law, or other handling that does not constitute a specific administrative act subject to lawsuit, after being signed or sealed by both parties, shall have the nature of a civil contract, unless otherwise provided by law.

9. If a party who has not entered into an arbitration agreement applies to the arbitration commission for mediation of a civil dispute, and after mediation is conducted by a specialized mediation organization established by the arbitration commission in accordance with fair and neutral mediation rules, a mediation agreement containing civil rights and obligations content is reached, and upon signature or seal by both parties, it shall have the nature of a civil contract.

10. The people's court encourages and supports industry associations, social organizations, enterprises, institutions, and others to establish and improve functions and mechanisms for mediating related disputes. A mediation agreement containing civil rights and obligations content reached after mediation by a commercial mediation organization, industry mediation organization, or other organization with mediation functions, after being signed or sealed by both parties, shall have the nature of a civil contract.

11. A labor dispute mediation agreement reached through mediation by a mediation organization as stipulated in the Labor Dispute Mediation and Arbitration Law of the PRC shall, after being signed or sealed by both parties, signed by the mediator, and sealed by the mediation organization, become effective and have contractual binding force on both parties, who shall perform it. The parties may, without going through arbitration proceedings, directly apply to the people's court for judicial confirmation of the validity of the mediation agreement in accordance with the provisions of these Opinions on judicial confirmation. If the people's court does not confirm it, the parties may apply to the labor dispute arbitration commission for arbitration.

12. For an agreement with payment content reached after mediation of a civil dispute by an administrative organ, people's mediation organization, commercial mediation organization, industry mediation organization, or other organization with mediation functions, the parties may apply to a notary public to grant compulsory enforcement effect in accordance with the provisions of the Notarization Law of the PRC. If the debtor fails to perform or improperly performs a notarial document with compulsory enforcement effect, the creditor may apply to the competent people's court for enforcement in accordance with the law.

13. For a mediation agreement with contractual effect and payment content, the creditor may apply to the competent basic people's court for a payment order in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and relevant judicial interpretations. The application shall state the amount of money or negotiable instruments requested, the facts and evidence on which it is based, and attach the original mediation agreement.

If a mediation agreement is reached on matters such as arrears of labor remuneration, work-related injury medical expenses, economic compensation, or damages, and the employer fails to perform within the period agreed in the agreement, the worker may apply to the people's court for a payment order in accordance with the law by presenting the mediation agreement.

III. Improve the Mediation Mechanism with Multi-Party Participation in Litigation Proceedings

14. For cases that fall within the scope of civil lawsuits accepted by the people's court and are under the jurisdiction of the accepting court, after receiving the statement of complaint or oral complaint but before formal case filing, the people's court may, ex officio or upon application by the parties, delegate mediation to an administrative organ, people's mediation organization, commercial mediation organization, industry mediation organization, or other organization with mediation functions. If the parties do not agree to mediation or fail to reach a mediation agreement within the agreed or specified time, the people's court shall file the case promptly in accordance with the law.

15. With the consent of both parties, or if the people's court deems it truly necessary, after case filing, the people's court may entrust a civil case to an administrative organ, people's mediation organization, commercial mediation organization, industry mediation organization, or other organization with mediation functions to assist in mediation. The parties may negotiate and select the relevant organ or organization, or may consult with the people's court to determine one.

After mediation, the relevant organ or organization shall inform the people's court of the mediation result. If a mediation agreement is reached, the parties may apply for withdrawal of the lawsuit, apply for judicial confirmation, or the people's court may issue a mediation statement after review. If mediation fails, the people's court shall proceed to trial promptly.

16. For a civil case that has been filed, the people's court may, in accordance with relevant provisions, invite qualified organizations or individuals to conduct mediation jointly with the trial panel. Mediation shall be conducted in a courtroom or other office premises of the people's court, or with the consent of the parties, may be conducted outside the court. If a mediation agreement is reached, the parties may be allowed to withdraw the lawsuit, or the people's court may issue a mediation statement after review. If mediation fails, the people's court shall proceed to trial promptly.

In principle, a judge who conducts mediation before trial shall not participate in the trial of the same case, unless the parties agree otherwise.

17. When an organization mediates a case, provided that it does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, it may refer to industry practices, village rules and folk conventions, community covenants, local good customs, and other behavioral norms to guide the parties in reaching a mediation agreement.

18. If a party conceals important facts, provides false information, or intentionally delays time during the mediation process, the mediator may issue a warning or terminate the mediation, and report the matter to the delegating or entrusting people's court. If the party's actions cause losses to other parties or third parties, it shall bear corresponding legal liability.

19. The mediation process shall not be open to the public, unless both parties request or agree to public mediation.

The organs, organizations, and mediators engaged in mediation, as well as court staff responsible for mediation case management, shall not disclose relevant information about the mediation process, and shall not testify in litigation proceedings related to the case. The parties shall not present as evidence in the trial proceedings any records made during the mediation process, concessions or commitments made by the parties to reach a mediation agreement, or any opinions or suggestions made by the mediator or the parties, except in the following circumstances:

(1) Both parties agree;
(2) Explicitly provided by law;
(3) The people's court deems it necessary to protect national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of third parties.

IV. Standardize and Improve the Judicial Confirmation Procedure

20. For an agreement with the nature of a civil contract reached after mediation by an administrative organ, people's mediation organization, commercial mediation organization, industry mediation organization, or other organization with mediation functions, after being signed and sealed by the mediation organization and the mediator, the parties may apply to the competent people's court for confirmation of its validity. If a party requests performance, modification, or rescission of the mediation agreement, or requests a declaration that the mediation agreement is void, it may file a lawsuit with the people's court.

21. The parties may, in the written mediation agreement, choose the basic people's court of the place of domicile of one party, the place of performance of the mediation agreement, the place where the mediation agreement was signed, or the location of the subject matter to have jurisdiction, provided that it does not violate the mandatory provisions on exclusive jurisdiction. If the parties have not agreed, subject to the circumstances provided in Article 34 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, jurisdiction shall lie with the basic people's court of the place of domicile of one party or the place of performance of the mediation agreement. For cases applying for confirmation of mediation agreements reached through mediation delegated or entrusted by the people's court to relevant organs or organizations, jurisdiction shall lie with the delegating or entrusting people's court.

22. The parties shall jointly apply to the competent people's court for confirmation in writing or orally. If one party applies and the other party expresses consent, it shall be deemed as a joint application. When applying, the parties shall submit the mediation agreement and a letter of undertaking to the people's court. Upon receiving the application, the people's court shall promptly review it. If the materials are complete, it shall promptly serve an acceptance notice on the parties. The letter of undertaking signed by both parties shall clearly state the following:

(1) Both parties voluntarily reached the agreement for the purpose of resolving the dispute, without malicious collusion or acts to circumvent the law;
(2) If the content of the agreement causes harm to others, they are willing to bear corresponding civil liability and other legal liability.

23. When hearing a case for application for confirmation of a mediation agreement, the people's court shall refer to the provisions on summary procedures in the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. The case shall be tried by a single judge, and both parties shall appear in court simultaneously. The people's court shall inquire face-to-face whether both parties understand the content of the agreement reached, whether they accept the consequences arising therefrom, and whether they are willing for the court to grant compulsory enforcement effect to the agreement through the judicial confirmation procedure.

24. In any of the following circumstances, the people's court shall not confirm the validity of the mediation agreement:

(1) Violation of mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations;
(2) Infringement of national interests or public interests;
(3) Infringement of the lawful rights and interests of third parties;
(4) Involving whether to pursue the criminal liability of a party;
(5) Content is unclear and cannot be confirmed or enforced;
(6) The mediation organization or mediator forced mediation or engaged in other serious violations of professional ethics standards;
(7) Other circumstances where confirmation should not be granted.

If a party signs a mediation agreement against its true intention, or if the mediation organization or mediator has an interest in the case or the mediation is manifestly unfair, the people's court shall not confirm the validity of the mediation agreement, unless the party knew of the existence of the above circumstances but still insisted on applying for confirmation.

25. After review in accordance with the law, the people's court shall decide whether to confirm the validity of the mediation agreement. The decision confirming the validity of the mediation agreement shall become legally effective upon service on both parties. If one party refuses to perform, the other party may apply to the people's court for enforcement in accordance with the law.

V. Establish and Improve Working Mechanisms

26. Where conditions permit, local people's courts may establish rosters of mediation organizations and mediators according to certain standards, so as to guide parties in choosing appropriate mediation organizations or mediators to mediate disputes. The people's court may adjust the rosters of mediation organizations and mediators in a timely manner based on specific circumstances.

27. Mediators shall abide by the professional ethics standards for mediators. If, in the course of handling related cases, the people's court discovers that a mediator has an interest in the case being mediated that may affect the mediator's ability to maintain neutrality and fair mediation, or if the mediator has other acts violating professional ethics standards, the people's court shall inform the mediator to withdraw, replace the mediator, terminate the mediation, or take other appropriate measures. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the people's court shall not allow a mediator who has participated in mediation to later act as an agent of a party in litigation proceedings concerning the same dispute or related disputes.

28. As needed for the work, the people's court shall designate internal units or personnel responsible for managing and coordinating communication, liaison, training, and guidance with mediation organizations and mediators.

29. People's courts at all levels shall strengthen contacts with other state organs, social organizations, enterprises, institutions, and related organizations, encourage innovation in various non-litigation dispute resolution mechanisms, participate in the construction of various non-litigation dispute resolution mechanisms through appropriate means, rationalize various relationships arising in the process of linking litigation and non-litigation, and actively promote the establishment and improvement of various non-litigation dispute resolution mechanisms.

30. Local people's courts at various levels shall, based on actual circumstances, formulate norms concerning mediator qualifications, professional ethics, mediation costs, allocation of litigation costs, mediation management, mediation guidance, and connection methods. Relevant work norms formulated by higher people's courts shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for record. Relevant work norms formulated by basic people's courts and intermediate people's courts shall be reported to the higher people's court for record.
